title: The nuns first (Prouille, 1206)
hookLine: Dominic's first community was of women

cards: Ask who the first Dominicans were, and you may picture men: friars in white and black, walking to the cities, preaching in the squares.
But go back to the south of France, to a small place called Prouille, at the foot of a hill.
Before there was an Order of Preachers, before the pope had approved anything, Dominic and his bishop Diego gathered a household there. Not of preachers. Of women.
They prayed, they worked, they lived together behind walls. Today, the community that came before the friars.

teach.b: Why women? The reason is in Jordan of Saxony's account.
In that region, he says, some families who were noble but poor had handed their daughters to the Cathars to be raised and taught, because they couldn't provide for them.
When women like these came back to the Catholic faith, they had nowhere to go.
So Diego and Dominic founded a monastery at Prouille to receive them. It became the first house of what grew into the Dominican family. The friars came after.
That's an odd start for an order of preachers: its first community didn't preach in the streets at all. It prayed.
Dominicans sometimes speak of their nuns' prayer as going before the friars' words. A preacher walking into a hostile town at dawn has someone already praying for him.
And the Gospel has its own women who came first in their way.
Luke tells how women traveled with Jesus and the Twelve: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna and others, in the Douay-Rheims, "who ministered unto him of their substance."

teach.h: WOMEN WHO PAID FOR THE ROAD.
WHO MINISTERED UNTO HIM OF THEIR SUBSTANCE.
teach.b: Luke places them at the cross, and at the empty tomb. At Prouille too, women are the first chapter: before the order had a name, a rule or a pope's approval, it had a house of women praying.

how: Dominican nuns live enclosed lives of prayer, study and work in monasteries, praying especially for the preaching of the friars; Dominicans honor Prouille as the first house of their family.

games.q: you're Dominic, preaching in Cathar country. women raised in Cathar houses are coming back to the Catholic faith, and they have nowhere to live. what do you build first?
o: a school to train men as preachers.
a monastery to receive the women.
a church for your own preaching.
games.why: with Diego, he founded the monastery at Prouille. Dominic's first community was of women at prayer; the friars came after.

practice: Bring to mind a woman who prayed for you, or held you in her thoughts, before you knew it: a grandmother, a mother, an aunt, a teacher, a neighbor, a nun at a school you went to.

Like Joanna and Susanna giving of their substance, remember one concrete thing she gave, a meal, a ride, an evening, a few dollars, a word at the right time, and hold it; if you pray, thank God for her by name, and if not, say her name and the gift slowly to yourself.

wordCard.voice: The nuns first. At Prouille, Dominic's first community was a house of women at prayer, before there were any friars. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the Holy Preaching, a name used for the early community around Prouille.

carryVoice: Your line: the nuns came first. Before the friars set out, a house of women was already praying. I'll be here tomorrow.
